From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@auriga.com>

Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 09:15:00 -0400
Subject: Request: sub-60ms p95 for inference during peak window

Hi Dylan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the generative quality looks promising. Auriga is preparing a pilot for our customer-facing API that must meet a firm response-time target for a high-value vertical (real-time recommendations).

We have an ask: can Redwood commit to a p95 endpoint latency of <=60ms for the EU region during our daily peak window (08:00–20:00 CET) for the first 3 months of the pilot? The traffic shape will be steady but bursty during certain events. We understand this is tighter than standard hosted SLOs; we are prepared to discuss reserved capacity and longer-term commitments.

Can you put together a proposal of options (hosted with prioritized routing, Dedicated pool sizing, fallback model variants) and an operational runbook that shows failover behavior and observability?

Procurement will also need an outline of SLA credits and escalation paths. Attaching our internal timeline.

Best,
Emma Jones
Senior Product, Auriga Systems
Attachments: auriga_slo_request_20280612.pdf

Team — forwarding Auriga's ask (attached). High level: they want p95 <=60ms EU peak for 3 months. This is below our typical hosted guarantee. Options on the table:

- Dedicated GPU pool (reserved) with prioritized routing
- Model quantization + shorter context and top-k sampling to reduce inference time
- Canary traffic shaping and a staged SLA with a credit schedule

Immediate asks:
1) Priyom — can you ballpark throughput & pool sizing for sustained 150 qps with 3x burst headroom for the target latency? Mark assumptions.
2) Grace — product constraints: can we offer a temporary SLO variance and what telemetry/runbook must exist to sign off?
3) Laura — sales: we'll need a pricing anchor and recommended contract language for escalation and credits.

I've attached a quick spreadsheet with traffic assumptions (proposed-dedicated-architecture.xlsx). Please reply with answers or edits by EOD Thu so I can give Auriga a timeline.

Thanks — Dylan

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai

Date: Wed, 13 Jun 2028 09:40:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: sub-60ms p95 for inference during peak window

On Tue, Jun 12, 2028 at 10:02 AM dylan_brooks@redwood.ai wrote:
> Team — forwarding Auriga's ask (attached). High level: they want p95 <=60ms EU peak for 3 months.

Quick technical read: not impossible but depends on model and sequence length. If they use a 8k-context LLM with batch sizes >8, hitting p95 60ms on GPU is challenging at 150 qps unless we use higher-end cards (A100/4xA10) and aggressive batching limits or a distilled/quantized variant.

Assumptions I'd need from Auriga: average token length per request, model choice (we can propose a trimmed variant), and whether we can do prefix caching for repeated prompts. With conservative estimates (avg 60 tokens, typical open-source 7B refactor), recommended Dedicated pool: 6 x A10s with continous batching cap at 12 and dynamic scaling to 10 for bursts. That gets us to ~45–55ms median; p95 might still be ~75–90ms unless we reduce context or move to lower-precision kernels (int8).

Risks:
- Underprovisioning during bursts (we need burst buffer policy)
- Regression in generation quality if we quantize too much

I'll draft a short runbook for canary steps and what metrics we need (p50/p95/p99, kv cache hit rate, queue depth).

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 14:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: sub-60ms p95 for inference during peak window

Thanks for the notes. Short product/ops perspective: we can support a temporary, scoped SLO variance for a strategic pilot if the following are met:

- Dedicated pool commit for pilot duration (at least 3 months) with explicit sizing + burst policy
- Canary plan (start with 5% traffic ramp over 48h, verify kv-cache and tracing, then ramp to 100% over 3 days)
- Observability hooks: per-route p95 dashboards, synthetic probes, and automated rollback at threshold breach (>3 regressions in 24h)
- Agreed fallbacks: automatic downgrade to a compatible model variant with documented quality delta and a customer-facing message template

I added the runbook draft here: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/1a2B_Auriga-SLOs (see "canary_runbook.md"). Legal & finance will need the credit schedule; product can sign off on the pilot if infra confirms feasibility and we get an explicit engineering-owner for on-call during the pilot.

I'll be available for a 30-min sync Mon to walk through the runbook.

— Grace
Grace O'Connor
Product Manager, Redwood Inference

- Commercial: pilot pricing + reserved capacity fee; SLA credit schedule for repeated breaches (to be included in contract)
